missions.objective: 侦察本地 canary 服务 (http://localhost:4100) 的下单/库存相关接口：抓取并解析 /openapi.json，产出 (1) 下单接口的 method+path、请求体/参数 schema 与必填字段样例，(2) 库存查询接口与订单查询接口，(3) 是否存在 reset/seed/clear 之类的状态重置接口（若无可用的替代手段，如通过新商品或明确初始库存的方式），(4) 库存数据模型：商品/库存/订单如何关联，库存是否有唯一标识，(5) 是否存在鉴权（api key/token/无鉴权）。只做只读侦察：可以 GET /openapi.json、GET 库存、GET 订单列表，以及为了确认接口可用性最多发起极少量（≤3）的探测请求；不要做并发压测，不要下单大量商品。产出要写成可直接给执行器用的接口清单（含 curl 示例与 JSON 字段名）。

验证 POST /orders 在并发下是否超卖。步骤: (1) POST /reset 带 body {"stock":{"p5":3}} 把已知商品库存置为已知值（p5 为种子商品，库存 3；若 reset 不接受 p5 则用 p3 置为 10 并在报告中说明）；(2) 用 GET /products/p5 确认初始库存；(3) 并发发出远大于库存的 POST /orders 请求（body {"productId":"p5","qty":1}），并发度至少 20，总请求数 ≥ 60，记录每个响应的状态码（201/409/5xx/超时）与耗时；(4) 并发结束后用 GET /products/p5 读最终库存、GET /orders 统计成功订单数；(5) 判定：成功订单数 > 初始库存 即超卖（违反规格“库存永不低于 0”）；成功订单数 < 初始库存 即库存泄漏（下单失败但库存被扣）。必须给出原始证据：请求总数、201 计数、409 计数、错误计数、初始与最终库存、超卖/泄漏差值、并发参数（并发度/总请求数）。若发现超卖，再跑一次相同参数确认可复现，并给出最小复现步骤。

用同一个服务的第二个共享配额资源交叉验证同一类竞态：POST /coupons/{code}/claim 在并发下是否超发。步骤: (1) POST /reset（可不带 body 或按需）使 coupon SAVE10 配额回到已知值 5，GET /coupons/SAVE10 确认 {quota:5, remaining:5}；(2) 并发（并发度 ≥ 10，总请求数 ≥ 30）调用 POST /coupons/SAVE10/claim，记录每个状态码（201 claimed / 409 quota exhausted / 其他）；(3) 结束后 GET /coupons/SAVE10 读 remaining；(4) 判定：201 数量 > 初始 quota 即超发（违反“remaining 永不低于 0”），或 remaining ≠ quota - 成功数 即状态不一致。给出原始计数与并发参数。
Distill a draft template from intent i-20261026-0029fb

独立验证 POST /coupons/SAVE10/claim 在并发下是否超领（over-claim）。步骤：(1) POST /reset → GET /coupons/SAVE10 记录起始 {quota, remaining}；(2) 串行对照组：并发度 1、连续发 20 次 claim，期望恰好 5×201 + 15×409、结束后 remaining=0；(3) 并发扫描：并发度 2/4/8/12（各轮总请求数 ≥36，必须远大于 quota=5），用真正并行的客户端（node:http 或等价，须实测并发生效：总耗时接近单请求量级；注意 xargs -P 会退化为串行、curl --parallel 会去重相同 URL，均不可用），记录每个响应的状态码与响应中的 remaining；(4) 每轮结束后 GET /coupons/SAVE10 读最终 remaining；(5) 判定并给出原始证据：每轮起始 remaining、#201、#409、#404、#5xx、最终 remaining、期望 remaining（起始−#201）、是否出现重复的 remaining 值（含单波内重复的具体数值）、并发参数与实测总耗时；(6) 若确认超领，至少 3 次相同参数复现并给出最小复现步骤。

claims.statement: POST /orders is the place-order endpoint; required body fields are productId (string) and qty (integer, minimum 1); it returns 201 with an Order {id, productId, qty, status in [placed,cancelled]} or 409 on insufficient stock, and the spec states stock is decremented by qty and never goes below zero.

Inventory is readable via GET /products (paginated: page>=1 default 1, size 1..100 default 3) returning ProductPage {items[{id,name,price,stock}], page, size, total, pages}, and a single product via GET /products/{id} (404 {"error":"product not found"} when absent); orders via GET /orders returning {"items":[...]}.

A state-reset endpoint exists: POST /reset with optional body {"stock":{<productId>:<int>}} to override stock per product id, returning 200; it is the only reset/seed/clear path in the spec (GET /reset is 404, so it is POST-only).

The service is unauthenticated: /openapi.json declares no securitySchemes and every read endpoint (/, /health, /products, /products/{id}, /orders, /coupons/{code}) returned 200 with no api key or token supplied.

claims.minimal_repro: curl -s 'http://localhost:4100/products?page=1&size=100'  # total=7, only 6 items; curl -s 'http://localhost:4100/products/p7'  # 200 Whatsit
claims.statement: GET /products is inconsistent with its own total/pages metadata: with size=100 the response is {"items":[p1..p6],"total":7,"pages":1} (6 items, total claims 7), and GET /products/p7 returns a valid product (Whatsit, stock 40) that never appears in any page — page=3&size=3 and page=2&size=6 are empty; this violates the spec assertion 'Every product appears on exactly one page'.

Every response carries the header x-consistency: sync, suggesting stock decrement is intended to be synchronous (a hypothesis the oversell test must falsify), and the seed stock values are p1=10, p2=5, p3=100, p4=25, p5=3, p6=12, p7=40 (p7 unlisted).

Additional coupon endpoints exist for a second shared-quota resource: GET /coupons/{code} (200 {code,quota,remaining}, 404 unknown) and POST /coupons/{code}/claim (201 claimed, 409 quota exhausted, 'remaining never goes below zero'); seeded coupon SAVE10 has quota 5, remaining 5. /coupons (list) is 404 and there is no GET /orders/{id}.

capability_issues: No write-capable client at R1: I could not invoke POST /reset or POST /orders, so I could not empirically confirm the reset endpoint's effect or the order response shape. A capability to issue a small, authorized set of state-changing probes (and to restore state via POST /reset) is needed for the executor's oversell test.

The bash tool bundles multiple commands into one 'operation' and the kernel denied mixed bundles as R2; a granularity where a read-only GET is never bundled with anything write-like would avoid spurious denials during recon.

envelope.self_assessment: Read-only recon complete on all 5 objective points, though reset (3) is spec-only because R1 blocked the POST. I discovered a genuine pagination/listing defect in /products while doing routine inventory reads, which is directly relevant: the executor should use GET /products/p1..p7 for ground-truth stock (p7 is invisible to the list) and POST /reset to pin initial stock. All 7 endpoints and the two shared-quota resources (stock, coupon remaining) are enumerated with curl examples. envelope.summary: Recon of the local canary service at http://localhost:4100 succeeded: /openapi.json is served directly (200, OpenAPI 3.0.3, title "Canary inventory/order service"). I mapped the order/stock/coupon/product endpoints, their schemas and required fields, confirmed there is no auth (no securitySchemes, all GETs succeed unauthenticated), and found a state-reset endpoint (POST /reset, spec-only — R1 denied me from invoking it). While reading inventory I found a real listing inconsistency: products?size=100 reports total=7/pages=1 but returns only 6 items, and GET /products/p7 exists (Whatsit, stock 40) yet is never listed on any page. All responses carry x-consistency: sync.

Confirmed a concurrency oversell defect in POST /orders on http://localhost:4100. With p5 seeded to stock=3 via POST /reset and 80 qty=1 orders at concurrency 40, 28-42 orders were accepted (HTTP 201) per clean run, i.e. 25-39 more than stock — 5/5 identical runs failed. The defect is concurrency-specific: the identical request set issued sequentially placed exactly 3 orders (spec held), while the same client fired in parallel placed up to 80/80. Oracle self-checks passed (sensitive to a seeded racy reference, specific to a conformant reference). The SUT is shared with other missions, so every verdict uses a provably isolated measurement (all orders in GET /orders must be ones I created; contaminated attempts discarded and retried).
envelope.test_strength: 5x (80 requests, conc 40) primary runs + concurrency sweep at 1/5/20/40/80 (80 requests each) + minimal repro (4 concurrent, stock 1) + independent raw node:http cross-check (sequential vs parallel 40 reqs) + oracle sensitivity/specificity self-checks

deviations.expected: Each test_run is an independent measurement of the SUT.
deviations.observed: I launched six test_runs in one batch; they shared global SUT state (POST /reset clears orders AND restores stock) and interfered with each other, producing S4 bookkeeping anomalies (6x201 but 3 orders) and a setup failure. claims.statement: The oracle self-check demonstrates both sensitivity and specificity: the SAME oracle reports violations (R1,R2,R3; #201=36 > C=5) for an in-process racy reference and no violations for a mutex-serialised conformant reference (5x201 + 31x409, remaining [4,3,2,1,0], final 0).

claims.statement: Minor oracle-hygiene note: script 01 derives its expected accepted count from the SUT's own post-reset GET (seed.remaining) rather than from a spec constant; this is harmless here because the documented seed is quota=5 (confirmed by my independent harness, which hardcodes C=5 and still reproduces the defect), but the frozen scripts' capacity expectation is SUT-sourced.

integrity_issues: Script 01's `expect201`/`expect409` checks take the capacity from the SUT's own post-reset GET response (seed.remaining) instead of a spec constant; the independent oracle in oracle.mjs and my own harness both avoid this, so it did not affect any verdict.
envelope.test_strength: Concurrency exercised at K=2,4,8,12 with 36 parallel requests/round (frozen sweep), plus K=12/T=36 minimal repro x3 and an independent undici-fetch harness at K=16/T=30 x2; genuine parallelism evidenced by burst-time vs serial-equivalent speedups of 1.55-6.86x. Sequential controls run with 20 and 30 strictly serialised claims. Each measurement reset the SUT first and read start state (remaining=5) before the burst; runs executed one at a time to avoid cross-run contamination.
